   403	            let mut count = 0;
   404	            loop {
   405	                let page = tx.scan(name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256)?;
   406	                if page.is_empty() {
   407	                    break;
   408	                }
   409	                for (_, key) in page {
   410	                    let full = crate::key::decode(&key)
   411	                        .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Store("invalid activation index".into()))?;
   412	                    let group = full[..width].to_vec();
   413	                    bounds.after = Some(full);
   414	                    if nulls_distinct && group.contains(&Value::Null) {
   415	                        continue;
   416	                    }
   417	                    if previous.as_ref() == Some(&group) {
   418	                        count += 1;
   419	                    } else {
   420	                        previous = Some(group);
   421	                        count = 1;
   422	                    }
   423	                    if count > max {
   424	                        return Err(RuntimeError::Constraint(format!(
   425	                            "cannot activate {name}.{index}: existing group exceeds {max}"
   426	                        )));
   427	                    }
   428	                }
   429	            }
   430	        }
   431	    }
   432	    Ok(())
   433	}

   435	impl super::runner::Runner<'_> {
   436	    /// Authoritative adapters feed an ancestor-ordered batch to the ordinary
   437	    /// insert/update path; captures always resolve inside this transaction.
   438	    pub fn seed_server_rows(
   439	        &mut self,
   440	        rows: impl IntoIterator<Item = (String, Value)>,
   441	    ) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   442	        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
   443	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
   444	                "server seed requires system authority".into(),
   445	            ));
   446	        }
   447	        let order = self.schema.through_order();
   448	        let mut rows: Vec<_> = rows.into_iter().collect();
   449	        rows.sort_by_key(|(n, _)| order.iter().position(|x| x == n));
   450	        let count = rows.len() as u64;
   451	        for (name, row) in rows {
   452	            super::timeline::check_import(self.schema, &name)?;
   453	            // Adoption rewrites are system imports of stored images (LLP 3000.015 §1).
   454	            self.upsert(
   455	                &name,
   456	                &row.field("id")?.clone(),
   457	                row.import_input(&super::ImportInput(())),
   458	            )?;
   459	        }
   460	        self.check_final_exists()?;
   461	        Ok(count)
   462	    }
   463	
   464	    /// A bounded child-first sweep on the common Rows interface.
   465	    pub fn sweep_server_rows(&mut self, limit: usize, expiry_after: &mut BTreeMap<String, Vec<Value>>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
   466	        if !self.context.is_system() || self.device {
   467	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(
   468	                "server sweep requires system authority".into(),
   469	            ));
   470	        }
   471	        let now = self
   472	            .context
   473	            .now
   474	            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Input("sweep clock is not pinned".into()))?;
   475	        let mut count = 0;
   476	        let mut visited = 0;
   477	        let tables = resume_expiry_tables(self.schema.through_order().into_iter().rev().collect(), expiry_after);
   478	        for name in tables {
   479	            let Some((index, _)) = self.schema.tables[&name].expiry_index() else {
   480	                continue;
   481	            };
   482	            let due = Bounds { gte: Some(Value::Int(i64::MIN)), lte: Some(Value::Int(now)), ..Default::default() };
   483	            let mut bounds = due.clone();
   484	            bounds.after = expiry_after.get(&name).cloned();
   485	            let mut wrapped = bounds.after.is_none();
   486	            while visited < limit {
   487	                let batch = (limit - visited).min(256);
   488	                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, scope| {
   489	                    runner
   490	                        .tx
   491	                        .scan(scope, &name, index, &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, batch)
   492	                })?;
   493	                if page.is_empty() {
   494	                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
   495	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   496	                        bounds = due.clone();
   497	                        wrapped = true;
   498	                        continue;
   499	                    }
   500	                    break;
   501	                }
   502	                let page_len = page.len();
   503	                for (row, key) in page {
   504	                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&key);
   505	                    if let Some(after) = &bounds.after { expiry_after.insert(name.clone(), after.clone()); }
   506	                    visited += 1;
   507	                    mark_expiry_table(expiry_after, &name);
   508	                    match self.retire_expired_row(&name, &row) {
   509	                        Ok(true) => count += 1,
   510	                        Ok(false) => {},
   511	                        Err(RuntimeError::Structural { code: "E_REFERENCED" | "E_PARENT_HAS_CHILDREN", .. }) => {},
   512	                        Err(error) => return Err(error),
   513	                    }
   514	                }
   515	                if page_len < batch {
   516	                    expiry_after.remove(&name);
   517	                    if !wrapped && visited < limit {
   518	                        bounds = due.clone();
   519	                        wrapped = true;
   520	                        continue;
   521	                    }
   522	                    break;
   523	                }
   524	            }
   525	        }
   526	        Ok(count)
   527	    }
   528	}

   252	    pub(super) fn update(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, patch: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   253	        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].not_before.is_some() {
   254	            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(
   255	                "a mutation touching a `not before` table runs on the server".into(),
   256	            ));
   257	        }
   258	        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| {
   259	            runner.update_attempt(table_name, key, patch)
   260	        })
   261	    }

   263	    fn update_attempt(&mut self, table_name: &str, key: &Value, patch: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
   264	        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Update)?;

   266	        self.refuse_recorded(table_name, &patch)?;
   267	        super::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[table_name], table_name, &patch)?;
   268	        if patch.as_object()?.contains_key("id") {
   269	            return Err(RuntimeError::Input(format!("{table_name} update patch cannot change id")));
   270	        }
   271	        let id = key.as_str()?;
   272	        self.reserve_target_resolution(table_name, self.schema.table(table_name).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("missing table {table_name}")))?, &patch, false)?;
   273	        let Some(old) = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| {
   274	            runner.fetch_write_target(allowance, table_name, id)
   275	        })? else {
   276	            return Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()]));
   277	        };
   278	        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].sync.is_none() { return Err(self.write_miss(table_name, "byId", &[key.clone()])); }
   279	        let readable = !self.inactive_write_target(table_name, &old)?
   280	            && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, &old)?;
   281	        let patch = self.ignore_hidden_immutable_patch(table_name, patch, readable)?;
   282	        let (new, copy) = self.merge_patch(table_name, &old, &patch, readable)?;
   283	        self.replace(table_name, old, new, readable, &patch, copy)
   284	    }

   501	        // distinct entry prepaid its tree node, strings and this vector slot;
   502	        // the rows-written ceiling bounds the commit-end walk.

   510	        }
   511	        // The log's order must not depend on a map's iteration order.
   512	        let order = self.schema.through_order();

   515	            )

   377	    }

+#[test]
+fn legacy_semantic_backend_is_server_adoptable_but_device_refused() {
+    for (capability, source) in [
+        ("maintained-id-sha256-v1", "table entries:\n  group: text <=64\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .group\n  public\n"),
+        ("expiry-reference-actions-v1", "table parents:\n  until: time ?\n  expire at .until\n  public\ntable children:\n  parent: parents on delete cascade\n  cap 1 by parent\n  public\n"),
+    ] {
+        let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+        assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+        let backend = Backend { generation: 1, schema: bound.schema, programs: bound.programs.into_iter().map(|program| program.program).collect() };
+        let mut legacy = serde_json::to_value(&backend).unwrap();
+        for table in legacy["schema"]["tables"].as_object_mut().unwrap().values_mut() {
+            for constraint in table["constraints"].as_array_mut().unwrap() {
+                if let Some(names) = constraint.get_mut("Capabilities").and_then(|value| value.as_array_mut()) {
+                    names.retain(|value| value != capability);
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        let adopted: Schema = serde_json::from_value(legacy["schema"].clone()).unwrap();
+        assert!(adopted.legacy_semantic_capabilities.contains(capability));
+        assert!(serde_json::to_string(&adopted).unwrap().contains(capability));
+        let opening = Opening::parse(Some(&legacy.to_string())).expect("legacy bytes remain decodable for store migration");
+        let error = match opening.open(MemoryStore::new()) {
+            Err(error) => error,
+            Ok(_) => panic!("device executed backend missing {capability}"),
+        };
+        assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY");
+        assert!(error.to_string().contains(capability), "{error}");
+    }
+}
+
+fn legacy_digest_store<S: DeviceStore>(store: &mut S) -> Backend {
+    let source = "table entries:\n  group: text <=64\n  public\nview totals: count entries by .group\n  public\n";
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), source.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let mut current = Backend { generation: 2, schema: bound.schema, programs: bound.programs.into_iter().map(|program| program.program).collect() };
+    let mut legacy = serde_json::to_value(&current).unwrap();
+    legacy["generation"] = json!(1);
+    for table in legacy["schema"]["tables"].as_object_mut().unwrap().values_mut() {
+        for constraint in table["constraints"].as_array_mut().unwrap() {
+            if let Some(names) = constraint.get_mut("Capabilities").and_then(|value| value.as_array_mut()) {
+                names.retain(|value| value != "maintained-id-sha256-v1");
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    let old: Backend = serde_json::from_value(legacy.clone()).unwrap();
+    store.install(&old.schema, &BTreeMap::from([
+        ("device:backend".into(), legacy.to_string()),
+        ("device:generation".into(), "1".into()),
+    ]), false).unwrap();
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    tx.outbox_insert(1, "pending", r#"{"id":"pending","seq":1,"op":"write","args":{},"new_ids":[]}"#).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    current.generation = 2;
+    current
+}
+
+fn legacy_digest_recovery<S: DeviceStore>(store: &mut S, initial: bool) {
+    let current = legacy_digest_store(store);
+    let error = match Opening::Kept.open(Borrowed(store)) {
+        Err(error) => error,
+        Ok(_) => panic!("offline device executed a kept pre-digest backend"),
+    };
+    assert_eq!(error.code(), "E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY");
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    let before = tx.outbox_entries().unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    let opening = if initial { Opening::Initial(current) } else { Opening::Install(current) };
+    drop(opening.open(Borrowed(store)).expect("a current backend must recover a kept legacy backend"));
+    let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(tx.outbox_entries().unwrap(), before, "semantic upgrade preserves queued writes");
+    assert_eq!(tx.meta("device:generation").unwrap().as_deref(), Some("2"));
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn current_backend_recovers_kept_legacy_semantics_memory() {
+    for initial in [false, true] {
+        legacy_digest_recovery(&mut MemoryStore::new(), initial);
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn current_backend_recovers_kept_legacy_semantics_sqlite() {
+    for initial in [false, true] {
+        let host = common::Sqlite::new(if initial { "legacy-semantic-initial" } else { "legacy-semantic-install" });
+        legacy_digest_recovery(&mut snapback4_core::store::Store::open(&host.path("device")).unwrap(), initial);
+    }
+}

 rows, exactly like a predicted unique or cap refusal today: a child the
 server already deleted can refuse locally until its `del` arrives.
 
+The same completeness rule covers same-id insertion into a referenced table.
+A logical device miss does not prove that the server lacks an expired physical
+predecessor whose retirement would cascade or clear held children. Unless the
+id was freshly controller-minted for this attempt, the device queues that
+insert without predicted rows and lets the server retire any predecessor and
+publish the complete action closure.
+
+Any schema in which an expiring table is referenced requires device capability
+`expiry-reference-actions-v1`. A pre-Wave-12 stored schema may open on the
+server for transactional adoption and is restamped when published, but an old
+device is refused at the compatibility handshake before it can predict the old
+retirement or same-id behavior.
+
 This queues more parent deletes than today (every parent whose children are
 private to other viewers). That is the sound behavior: today's local delete
 is "predicted" only because orphans were the semantics.

+#[test]
+fn expiry_reference_actions_upgrade_legacy_wire_and_fence_old_devices() {
+    let source = "table parents:\n  until: time ?\n  expire at .until\n  public\ntable children:\n  parent: parents on delete cascade\n  cap 1 by parent\n  public\n";
+    let schema = compile(source);
+    assert!(schema.required_capabilities().contains("reference-actions"));
+    assert!(schema.required_capabilities().contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1"));
+
+    let reference_only = compile(&source.replace("  until: time ?\n  expire at .until\n", ""));
+    assert!(reference_only.required_capabilities().contains("reference-actions"));
+    assert!(!reference_only.required_capabilities().contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1"));
+    let expiry_only = compile("table parents:\n  until: time ?\n  expire at .until\n  public\n");
+    assert!(!expiry_only.required_capabilities().contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1"));
+
+    // A kept pre-Wave-12 schema decodes for server adoption, then its next
+    // projection stamps the new device requirement.
+    let mut legacy = serde_json::to_value(&schema).unwrap();
+    for table in legacy["tables"].as_object_mut().unwrap().values_mut() {
+        for constraint in table["constraints"].as_array_mut().unwrap() {
+            if let Some(names) = constraint.get_mut("Capabilities").and_then(|value| value.as_array_mut()) {
+                names.retain(|value| value != "expiry-reference-actions-v1");
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    let upgraded: Schema = serde_json::from_value(legacy).unwrap();
+    assert!(serde_json::to_string(&upgraded).unwrap().contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1"));
+
+    let required = snapback4_core::device_protocol::compatibility(&upgraded.public_projection());
+    let mut old = snapback4_core::device_protocol::DeviceEngine::current();
+    old.version = "0.4.28".into();
+    old.capabilities.retain(|capability| capability != "expiry-reference-actions-v1");
+    let refusal = snapback4_core::device_protocol::check(Some(&old), &required).unwrap_err();
+    assert_eq!(refusal.code, "E_DEVICE_VERSION");
+    assert!(refusal.message.contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1"), "{refusal:?}");
+}

+/-- An eager snapshot of the declared table rows used while sweeping. A
+`Store` update is a functional closure over the previous store; repeatedly
+retiring rows through that representation retains an exponentially growing
+evaluation tree. Snapshotting after each successful retirement changes only
+the representation, while preserving table order and action sequencing. -/
+abbrev MaterialStore := Array (String × List Row)
+
+def materialRows (tables : List String) (s : Store) : MaterialStore :=
+  tables.toArray.map fun t => (t, s t)
+
+def MaterialStore.store (rows : MaterialStore) (fallback : Store) : Store := fun t =>
+  match rows.find? fun p => p.1 == t with
+  | some (_, rs) => rs
+  | none => fallback t
+
+-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — sweep each due root transactionally in table order.
 /-- Retire every due physical row. `restrict` retains that root but never
 stops later due keys; cascade and set-null are committed with the root. The
 model has no read-through retained-history rows, so every non-restricted due
 root can be retired immediately. -/
 def sweepExpired (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store :=
-  sch.tables.foldl (fun s td => (s td.name).foldl (fun s r =>
-    if expired td now r && stored s td.name r then
-      match refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s td.name r with
-      | .ok next => next
-      | .error (.refuse "E_REFERENCED") => s
-      | .error _ => s
-    else s) s) s
+  let tables := sch.tables.map (·.name)
+  let rows := sch.tables.foldl (fun rows td =>
+    let physical := rows.store s
+    (physical td.name).foldl (fun rows r =>
+      let physical := rows.store s
+      if expired td now r && stored physical td.name r then
+        match refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch physical now) physical td.name r with
+        | .ok next => materialRows tables next
+        | .error (.refuse "E_REFERENCED") => rows
+        | .error _ => rows
+      else rows) rows) (materialRows tables s)
+  rows.store s

+This commit-end rule also covers a source of a row-keyed maintained view. The
+source's final image first reaches normal maintenance, then its expired image
+is retired through the common action path in the same transaction. No derived
+maintenance shortcut may physically remove that source before closure
+preflight: doing so would bypass a live `restrict` child and could orphan a
+`cascade` or `set null` child. The source contribution and its retirement
+cancel within the transaction, so an already-expired birth never enters a
+committed count basis. The execution retains at most one retirement key per
+changed source row; its allocation is charged when first retained and the
+program's existing rows-written ceiling bounds the commit-end walk.
+
 A live `restrict` child, or a physically retained read-through child outside
 the cascade closure but below a row in it, keeps the expired root physically
 stored and the sweep continues to later due keys. A read-through child inside

+#[test]
+fn row_keyed_view_source_expiry_retires_through_reference_actions() {
+    let source = r#"
+table conversations:
+  public
+table members:
+  conversation: conversations
+  principal: principal
+  cap 4 by conversation
+  public
+table messages:
+  conversation: conversations
+  ordinal: int
+  sender: principal
+  until: time ?
+  expire at .until
+  public
+  update <- allow
+view unread: count messages by members m
+  where .conversation = m.conversation and .sender != m.principal
+table cascadeKids:
+  message: messages on delete cascade
+  cap 1 by message
+  public
+table nullableKids:
+  message: messages ? on delete set null
+  cap 1 by message
+  public
+table blockers:
+  message: messages
+  public
+mutation expire(message: messages):
+  update messages[message] { until: now }
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("conversations".into(), object([("id", id("c"))])),
+        ("members".into(), object([("id", id("member")), ("conversation", id("c")), ("principal", id("alice"))])),
+        ("messages".into(), object([("id", id("message")), ("conversation", id("c")), ("ordinal", Value::Int(1)), ("sender", id("bob")), ("until", Value::Null)])),
+        ("cascadeKids".into(), object([("id", id("cascade")), ("message", id("message"))])),
+        ("nullableKids".into(), object([("id", id("nullable")), ("message", id("message"))])),
+        ("blockers".into(), object([("id", id("blocker")), ("message", id("message"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("unread").unwrap()[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+
+    let context = || Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::from([("message".into(), id("message"))])).at(100);
+    let refused = e.mutate("expire", None, context()).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(refused.state, WriteState::Failed { ref why, .. } if why.code == "E_REFERENCED"), "{:?}", refused.state);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("messages").unwrap()[0].field("until").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("unread").unwrap()[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().len(), 1, "a refused commit rolls its cascade back");
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("message").unwrap(), &id("message"));
+
+    e.seed_delete("blockers", "blocker").unwrap();
+    let sent = e.mutate("expire", None, context()).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(sent.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", sent.state);
+    assert!(e.store().rows("messages").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert!(e.store().rows("cascadeKids").unwrap().is_empty());
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("nullableKids").unwrap()[0].field("message").unwrap(), &Value::Null);
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("unread").unwrap()[0].field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(0));
+}

     8	
     9	* **insert** — the insert rule judges the new image (`E_RULE`); a clash on

    11	  row, `if absent` returns null and an ordinary insert refuses `E_CONSTRAINT`

    14	  write; the update rule judges old and next. Denial is `E_RULE` on a readable
    15	  target and `NOT_FOUND` on an unreadable one; a missing target is
    16	  `NOT_FOUND`; an `if` condition on an unreadable target is `NOT_FOUND`, and a
    17	  false one on a readable target `E_CONFLICT`; a secondary unique clash is
    18	  `NOT_FOUND` (unreadable target), `E_RULE` (hidden colliding row) or
    19	  `E_CONSTRAINT`. An admitted update may change a hidden row; the result is

    21	* **upsert** — patches an existing target as an update; inserts an absent

   176	/-- Every reference that names table `t` and carries an action:

   194	
   195	/-- Breadth-first closure over `cascade` references, each row once; `fuel`

   197	def closure (sch : Schema) (s : Store) : Nat → List (String × Row) → List (String × Row) → List (String × Row)

   199	  | _ + 1, [], acc => acc

   234	  if restricted sch witnesses cl then throw (.refuse "E_REFERENCED")
   235	  else
   236	    let physical := cl.foldl (fun s (parent, row) => (referencing sch parent).foldl (fun s (child, col, action) =>
   237	      if action == .setNull then
   238	        ((witnesses child).filter fun k => names k col row.id && !inClosure cl child k).foldl
   239	          (fun s witness => match (s child).find? fun current => current.id == witness.id with
   240	            | some current =>
   241	              if names current col row.id then s.replaceRow child current (clearCol current col) else s
   242	            | none => s) s
   243	      else s) s) physical
   244	    pure (cl.foldl (fun s p => s.removeRow p.1 p.2) physical)

   246	/-! ## Expiry retirement (LLP 3000.036.003 §6; LLP 3000.039 §3) -/
   247	
   248	def expired (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool :=
   249	  match td.expire with
   250	  | none => false
   251	  | some c => match r.get c with
   252	    | .int closes => closes <= now
   253	    | _ => false
   254	
   255	def stored (s : Store) (t : String) (r : Row) : Bool :=
   256	  (s t).any fun current => current.id == r.id
   257	
   258	/-- Retire a due row that physically holds an inserted id. The native engine
   259	does this before checking the new image's remaining unique keys, in the same
   260	transaction as the insert. -/
   261	def retireExpiredSameId (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) (t : String)
   262	    (td : TableDecl) (rid : List Nat) : Except Stop Store :=
   263	  match findRow (s t) [("id", .id rid)] with
   264	  | some old =>
   265	    if expired td now old then refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch s now) s t old
   266	    else pure s
   267	  | none => pure s
   268	
   269	/-- Whether `insert if absent` has a live unique-key occupant. Native checks
   270	all live unique collisions before retiring an expired same-id predecessor, so
   271	a no-op leaves the physical store and its action children unchanged. -/
   272	def insertIfAbsentClash (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (now : Int)
   273	    (t : String) (td : TableDecl) (img : Row) : Except Stop Bool :=
   274	  match findClash ((s t).filter (unexpired td now)) (["id"] :: td.uniques) img none with
   275	  | some (_, r) => do
   276	    guardE (readableAt sch s v now t r) eRule
   277	    pure true
   278	  | none => pure false
   279	
   280	/-- An eager snapshot of the declared table rows used while sweeping. A
   281	`Store` update is a functional closure over the previous store; repeatedly
   282	retiring rows through that representation retains an exponentially growing
   283	evaluation tree. Snapshotting after each successful retirement changes only
   284	the representation, while preserving table order and action sequencing. -/
   285	abbrev MaterialStore := Array (String × List Row)
   286	
   287	def materialRows (tables : List String) (s : Store) : MaterialStore :=
   288	  tables.toArray.map fun t => (t, s t)
   289	
   290	def MaterialStore.store (rows : MaterialStore) (fallback : Store) : Store := fun t =>
   291	  match rows.find? fun p => p.1 == t with
   292	  | some (_, rs) => rs
   293	  | none => fallback t
   294	
   295	/-- Runtime's stable ancestor order is lexical when read-through is absent,
   296	as it is in this model fragment. Expiry retirement visits that order in
   297	reverse so peers cannot depend on declaration or mutation order. -/
   298	def expiryRetirementTables (sch : Schema) : List TableDecl :=
   299	  sch.tables.mergeSort fun a b => String.compare a.name b.name != .lt
   300	
   301	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — sweep each due root transactionally in table order.
   302	/-- Retire every due physical row. `restrict` retains that root but never
   303	stops later due keys; cascade and set-null are committed with the root. The
   304	model has no read-through retained-history rows, so every non-restricted due
   305	root can be retired immediately. -/
   306	def sweepExpired (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store :=
   307	  let tables := sch.tables.map (·.name)
   308	  let rows := (expiryRetirementTables sch).foldl (fun rows td =>
   309	    let physical := rows.store s
   310	    (physical td.name).foldl (fun rows r =>
   311	      let physical := rows.store s
   312	      if expired td now r && stored physical td.name r then
   313	        match refDeleteFrom sch (unexpiredStore sch physical now) physical td.name r with
   314	        | .ok next => materialRows tables next
   315	        | .error (.refuse "E_REFERENCED") => rows
   316	        | .error _ => rows
   317	      else rows) rows) (materialRows tables s)
   318	  rows.store s
   319	
   320	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#6 — same-id replacement authorizes, retires with actions, then inserts.
   321	/-- Apply one write to the store. -/
   322	def applyWrite (cx : Ctx) (s : Store) : RWrite → Except Stop (Value × Store)
   323	  | .insert t fields ifAbsent =>
   324	    match cx.schema.table? t with
   325	    | none => throw eInput
   326	    | some td => do
   327	      let fs ← scalarsE fields
   328	      let rid ← insertId fs
   329	      let img ← buildImage td rid fs eInput
   330	      -- Native refusal order authorizes the proposed image while the expired
   331	      -- predecessor is still present, then retires it and applies its actions.
   332	      guardE (td.insert.eval (openedStore cx.schema s cx.now) cx.viewer { self := some img }) eRule
   333	      if ifAbsent then
   334	        let clashes ← insertIfAbsentClash cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img
   335	        if clashes then pure (.null, s)
   336	        else
   337	          let s ← retireExpiredSameId cx.schema s cx.now t td rid
   338	          doInsertImage cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img eRule
   339	      else
   340	        let s ← retireExpiredSameId cx.schema s cx.now t td rid
   341	        doInsertImage cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img eRule
   342	  | .update t key patch cond =>
   343	    match cx.schema.table? t with
   344	    | none => throw eInput
   345	    | some td => do
   346	      let ks ← scalarsE key
   347	      let ps ← scalarsE patch
   348	      match findLiveRow td cx.now (s t) ks with
   349	      | none => throw notFound
   350	      | some old => doUpdateRow cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td old ps cond
   351	  | .upsert t key patch =>
   352	    match cx.schema.table? t with
   353	    | none => throw eInput
   354	    | some td => do
   355	      let ks ← scalarsE key
   356	      let ps ← scalarsE patch
   357	      match findLiveRow td cx.now (s t) ks with
   358	      | some old => doUpdateRow cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td old ps none
   359	      | none => do
   360	        let rid ← upsertId ks ps
   361	        let img ← buildImage td rid (ks ++ ps) notFound
   362	        guardE (td.insert.eval (openedStore cx.schema s cx.now) cx.viewer { self := some img }) notFound
   363	        let s ← retireExpiredSameId cx.schema s cx.now t td rid
   364	        doInsertImage cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t td img notFound
   365	  | .delete t key =>
   366	    match cx.schema.table? t with
   367	    | none => throw eInput
   368	    | some td => do
   369	      let ks ← scalarsE key
   370	      match findLiveRow td cx.now (s t) ks with
   371	      | none => throw notFound
   372	      | some old => do
   373	        guardE (td.delete.eval (openedStore cx.schema s cx.now) cx.viewer { self := some old })

   375	        guardE ((referencing cx.schema t).isEmpty || readableAt cx.schema s cx.viewer cx.now t old) notFound
   376	        pure (.null, ← refDeleteFrom cx.schema (unexpiredStore cx.schema s cx.now) s t old)
   377	
   378	end Quarry

     1	import Quarry.Syntax

     3	/-!
     4	# Rows, stores, rules and visibility
     5	
     6	A store maps each table name to its rows. Rules are evaluated against the
     7	whole store: an `exists t[..]` probe is an exact-key existence test that does
     8	not consult `t`'s own read rule (OPEN R1). A row is *visible* to a viewer
     9	when its table's read rule holds for it; every read the evaluator performs
    10	goes through `visibleRows`, so the read semantics in `Eval.lean` never sees
    11	a hidden row (`Disclosure.lean`).
    12	-/
    13	
    14	namespace Quarry
    15	
    16	structure Row where
    17	  id : List Nat
    18	  cols : List (String × Scalar)
    19	  deriving Repr, DecidableEq, Inhabited
    20	
    21	def Row.get (r : Row) (c : String) : Scalar :=
    22	  if c = "id" then .id r.id else (r.cols.lookup c).getD .null
    23	
    24	def Row.toValue (r : Row) : Value :=
    25	  .row (("id", .s (.id r.id)) :: r.cols.map fun p => (p.1, .s p.2))
    26	
    27	/-- The store: the rows of each table. -/
    28	abbrev Store := String → List Row
    29	
    30	def Store.empty : Store := fun _ => []
    31	
    32	def Store.set (s : Store) (t : String) (rs : List Row) : Store :=
    33	  fun t' => if t' = t then rs else s t'
    34	
    35	def Store.insertRow (s : Store) (t : String) (r : Row) : Store := s.set t (s t ++ [r])
    36	def Store.replaceRow (s : Store) (t : String) (old nw : Row) : Store :=
    37	  s.set t ((s t).map fun r => if r.id = old.id then nw else r)
    38	def Store.removeRow (s : Store) (t : String) (old : Row) : Store :=
    39	  s.set t ((s t).filter fun r => r.id ≠ old.id)
    40	
    41	/-- The images a rule may name. -/
    42	structure Imgs where
    43	  self : Option Row := none
    44	  old : Option Row := none
    45	  next : Option Row := none
    46	
    47	def Imgs.get (im : Imgs) : Img → Option Row
    48	  | .self => im.self
    49	  | .old => im.old
    50	  | .next => im.next
    51	
    52	def Term.eval (v : List Nat) (im : Imgs) : Term → Option Scalar
    53	  | .col i c => (im.get i).map (·.get c)
    54	  | .viewer => some (.id v)
    55	  | .param _ => none
    56	  | .lit x => some x
    57	
    58	/-- Evaluate every component of a key probe. -/
    59	def probeTerms (v : List Nat) (im : Imgs) (key : List (String × Term)) :
    60	    Option (List (String × Scalar)) :=
    61	  key.mapM fun p => Option.map (fun x => (p.1, x)) (p.2.eval v im)
    62	
    63	/-- Null returns no row only when it occurs in the selected unique point key.
    64	Nullable equalities outside that key are residual predicates and may match
    65	null. An empty `point` keeps the older all-components convention for the
    66	hand-written core model. -/
    67	def probeKey (v : List Nat) (im : Imgs) (point : List String)
    68	    (key : List (String × Term)) :
    69	    Option (List (String × Scalar)) :=
    70	  match probeTerms v im key with
    71	  | none => none
    72	  | some ks =>
    73	    let selected := if point.isEmpty then ks else ks.filter fun p => point.contains p.1
    74	    if selected.length == (if point.isEmpty then ks.length else point.eraseDups.length)
    75	        && !(selected.any fun p => p.2 == .null)
    76	    then some ks else none
    77	
    78	def keyMatch (ks : List (String × Scalar)) (r : Row) : Bool :=
    79	  ks.all fun p => decide (r.get p.1 = p.2)
    80	
    81	/-- Rule evaluation against the whole store `s`, for viewer `v`. -/
    82	def Rule.eval (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (im : Imgs) : Rule → Bool
    83	  | .allow => true
    84	  | .deny => false
    85	  | .eq a b => match a.eval v im, b.eval v im with
    86	    | some x, some y => decide (x = y)
    87	    | _, _ => false
    88	  | .ne a b => match a.eval v im, b.eval v im with
    89	    | some x, some y => decide (x ≠ y)
    90	    | _, _ => false
    91	  | .probe t point key => match probeKey v im point key with
    92	    | some ks => (s t).any (keyMatch ks)
    93	    | none => false
    94	  | .and a b => a.eval s v im && b.eval s v im
    95	  | .or a b => a.eval s v im || b.eval s v im
    96	  | .not a => !(a.eval s v im)
    97	
    98	/-- The tables a rule probes. -/
    99	def Rule.probes : Rule → List String
   100	  | .probe t _ _ => [t]
   101	  | .and a b | .or a b => a.probes ++ b.probes
   102	  | .not a => a.probes
   103	  | _ => []
   104	
   105	/-- The row columns (of the `self` image) a rule reads. -/
   106	def Term.selfCols : Term → List String
   107	  | .col .self c => [c]
   108	  | _ => []
   109	
   110	/-- Every term a rule compares or probes with, left to right. -/
   111	def Rule.terms : Rule → List Term
   112	  | .eq a b | .ne a b => [a, b]
   113	  | .probe _ _ key => key.map (·.2)
   114	  | .and a b | .or a b => a.terms ++ b.terms
   115	  | .not a => a.terms
   116	  | .allow | .deny => []
   117	
   118	def Rule.selfCols (r : Rule) : List String := r.terms.flatMap Term.selfCols
   119	
   120	/-- The rule with each term replaced by `f` of it. -/
   121	def Rule.mapTerms (f : Term → Term) : Rule → Rule
   122	  | .eq a b => .eq (f a) (f b)
   123	  | .ne a b => .ne (f a) (f b)
   124	  | .probe t point key => .probe t point (key.map fun p => (p.1, f p.2))
   125	  | .and a b => .and (a.mapTerms f) (b.mapTerms f)
   126	  | .or a b => .or (a.mapTerms f) (b.mapTerms f)
   127	  | .not a => .not (a.mapTerms f)
   128	  | .allow => .allow
   129	  | .deny => .deny
   130	
   131	/-- The disjuncts of a rule's top-level `or` (a rule that is not an `or` is
   132	its own single disjunct). -/
   133	def Rule.disjuncts : Rule → List Rule
   134	  | .or a b => a.disjuncts ++ b.disjuncts
   135	  | .allow => [.allow]
   136	  | .deny => [.deny]
   137	  | .eq a b => [.eq a b]
   138	  | .ne a b => [.ne a b]
   139	  | .probe t point key => [.probe t point key]
   140	  | .and a b => [.and a b]
   141	  | .not a => [.not a]
   142	
   143	/-- A rule without `not`. Over fewer rows a positive rule can only lose
   144	probe witnesses, so one true over the caller's view is true over the store
   145	(`Rule.eval_mono`); the engine likewise never takes a negated probe as a
   146	grant (LLP 3000.036 §12.1). -/
   147	def Rule.positive : Rule → Bool
   148	  | .not _ => false
   149	  | .and a b | .or a b => a.positive && b.positive
   150	  | .allow | .deny | .eq .. | .ne .. | .probe .. => true
   151	
   152	/-- Fold only rule truth values that remain known after pin substitution.
   153	Boolean literal comparisons match the engine's required-boolean pin proof;
   154	in particular, a nullable `null` pin is not treated as boolean `false`.
   155	Probes are never folded, so normalization cannot turn a negated probe into a
   156	page grant (LLP 3000.036 §14). -/
   157	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.001#9 — the formal classifier and executable model share prefix-normalized guards.
   158	def Rule.normalize : Rule → Rule
   159	  | .eq (.lit (.bool a)) (.lit (.bool b)) => if a == b then .allow else .deny
   160	  | .eq (.lit a) (.lit b) => if a == b then .allow else .eq (.lit a) (.lit b)
   161	  | .eq .viewer .viewer => .allow
   162	  | .eq a b => .eq a b
   163	  | .ne (.lit (.bool a)) (.lit (.bool b)) => if a != b then .allow else .deny
   164	  | .ne (.lit a) (.lit b) => if a != b then .ne (.lit a) (.lit b) else .deny
   165	  | .ne .viewer .viewer => .deny
   166	  | .ne a b => .ne a b
   167	  | .and a b =>
   168	      match a.normalize, b.normalize with
   169	      | .allow, b' => b'
   170	      | a', .allow => a'
   171	      | .deny, _ | _, .deny => .deny
   172	      | a', b' => .and a' b'
   173	  | .or a b =>
   174	      match a.normalize, b.normalize with
   175	      | .allow, _ | _, .allow => .allow
   176	      | .deny, b' => b'
   177	      | a', .deny => a'
   178	      | a', b' => .or a' b'

   180	      | .allow => .deny
   181	      | .deny => .allow
   182	      | a' => .not a'

   184	  | .deny => .deny

   187	/-- A term with each pinned row column replaced by its pinned value. -/
   188	def Term.pin (ps : List (String × Scalar)) : Term → Term

   190	    | some x => .lit x
   191	    | none => .col .self c

   194	/-- A rule with each pinned row column replaced by its pinned value: the
   195	verdict the rule gives every row the pins select (`Rule.eval_pin`). -/
   196	def Rule.pin (ps : List (String × Scalar)) (r : Rule) : Rule := r.mapTerms (Term.pin ps)
   197	
   198	def readable (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (t : String) (r : Row) : Bool :=
   199	  match sch.table? t with
   200	  | some td => td.read.eval s v { self := some r }
   201	  | none => false

   203	/-- The rows of `t` the viewer may read. Every read goes through this. -/
   204	def visibleRows (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (v : List Nat) (t : String) : List Row :=
   205	  (s t).filter (readable sch s v t)
   206	
   207	/-- Whether a row has reached its table's lower read lifetime. Null is open;
   208	the checked schema guarantees that a non-null lifetime value is a time. -/
   209	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#3-semantics — lower read lifetimes filter every logical read at the server clock.
   210	def opened (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool :=
   211	  match td.notBefore with
   212	  | none => true
   213	  | some c => match r.get c with
   214	    | .null => true
   215	    | .int opens => opens <= now
   216	    | _ => false
   217	
   218	/-- Whether a row remains before its table's upper read lifetime. Null has no
   219	upper bound; the checked schema guarantees that a non-null value is a time. -/
   220	-- @ref LLP 3000.036.003#3-semantics — upper read lifetimes filter every logical read before physical cleanup.
   221	def unexpired (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool :=
   222	  match td.expire with
   223	  | none => true

   226	    | .int closes => now < closes
   227	    | _ => false

   229	def live (td : TableDecl) (now : Int) (r : Row) : Bool := opened td now r && unexpired td now r
   230	
   231	/-- Referential actions ignore expired child images but still govern a child

   233	def unexpiredStore (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store := fun t =>
   234	  match sch.table? t with
   235	  | some td => (s t).filter (unexpired td now)
   236	  | none => []
   237	
   238	/-- The physical store with rows outside their logical lifetime removed. Rule
   239	probes use this store too, so a future or expired row cannot authorize work. -/
   240	def openedStore (sch : Schema) (s : Store) (now : Int) : Store := fun t =>
   241	  match sch.table? t with

   243	  | none => []

    27	/-- The world of a mutation: the store; reads see its visible rows. -/
    28	def storeHooks : Hooks Store where

    37	
    38	structure MutationWorld where

    42	/-- The explicit address of an insert-like write that reached its write arm.

    45	def RWrite.changedExplicitId? (cx : Ctx) (s : Store) : RWrite → Option (String × List Nat)

    63	def changedFinalRows (sch : Schema) (before after : Store) : ChangedRows :=

    65	    match (before td.name).find? fun old => old.id == row.id with
    66	    | none => some (td.name, row.id)
    67	    | some old => if old == row then none else some (td.name, row.id)

    69	def mutationHooks : Hooks MutationWorld where

   111	        // A format change can leave schema/program bytes unchanged.

   114	            return Err(RuntimeError::Store("not this Postgres evaluation store version".into()));

     5	pub(super) fn install(tx: &Tx<'_>, schema: &mut Schema) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
     6	    let backend = tx.query("SELECT schema,generation FROM _backend WHERE singleton", &[])?;

    11	        for (name, table) in &schema.tables {
    12	            for (index_name, index) in &table.indexes {
    13	                let Some(IndexComponent::Contribution(maintain)) = index.components.first() else {continue};
    14	                if previous.table(name).and_then(|t|t.index(index_name)) == Some(index) {continue;}
    15	                tx.execute("DELETE FROM i WHERE t = $1 AND ix = $2", &[name,index_name])?;
    16	                let work=adoption::Work::DECODE.with_contribution(maintain);
    17	                let mut after: Option<String> = None;
    18	                loop {
    19	                    let mut meter=Meter::new(Ceilings::job(),Cut::Abort);
    20	                    meter.at(&format!("adopt {name}.{index_name}"));
    21	                    meter.heap(4096 + after.as_deref().map_or(0, heap::text))?;
    22	                    let page=source_page(&tx,name,table,after.as_deref(),&mut meter,work)?;
    23	                    if page.is_empty() { break; }
    24	                    for raw in &page {
    25	                        let scratch=meter.mark();
    26	                        let id=raw.get::<_,&str>(0);
    27	                        let data=raw.get::<_,&str>(1);
    28	                        meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined,1)?;
    29	                        adoption::charge(&mut meter, adoption::decode_bytes(data))?;
    30	                        let row: Value=super::store::decode(data)?;
    31	                        meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined,1)?;
    32	                        meter.step(maintain.evaluation_steps())?;
    33	                        adoption::charge(&mut meter, adoption::contribution_bytes(&row,table))?;
    34	                        for key in crate::rows::stored_index_keys(table,index,&row,id) {
    35	                            if key.len() > crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES { return Err(crate::rows::index_key_refusal(name,index_name,1)); }
    36	                            meter.charge(MeterKind::IndexEntries,1)?;
    37	                            tx.execute("INSERT INTO i(t,ix,k,id) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4)", &[name,index_name,&key,&id])?;
    38	                        }

    58	pub(super) fn source_page(tx: &super::store::Tx<'_>, table: &str, schema: &Table, after: Option<&str>, meter: &mut Meter, work: adoption::Work) -> Result<Vec<postgres::Row>, RuntimeError> {
    59	    let sizes=if after.is_some() {
    60	        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(octet_length(id) + octet_length(data)),0)::bigint, COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND id>$2 ORDER BY id LIMIT $3) AS picked"
    61	    } else {
    62	        "SELECT COALESCE(SUM(octet_length(id) + octet_length(data)),0)::bigint, COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND $2::text IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT $3) AS picked"
    63	    };
    64	    let mut limit=32i64;
    65	    let page_mark=meter.mark();
    66	    loop {
    67	        limit=work.limit(meter,limit as usize) as i64;
    68	        let size=tx.query(sizes,&[&table,&after,&limit])?;
    69	        let bytes=size[0].get::<_,i64>(0) as u64;
    70	        let count=size[0].get::<_,i64>(1) as u64;
    71	        // Network/read buffers, retained driver rows and their metadata. Typed
    72	        // JSON decode is priced from borrowed text later, one row at a time;
    73	        // the query scan's conservative 256x all-rows decoder is inappropriate
    74	        // for this walk. This initial estimate is followed by a scratch check
    75	        // before any adoption callback runs.
    76	        let reservation=bytes.saturating_mul(8).saturating_add(count.saturating_mul(1024));
    77	        if limit>1 && reservation>meter.ceilings.heap_bytes/2 { limit/=2; continue; }
    78	        meter.heap(reservation)?;
    79	        let query=if after.is_some() {
    80	            "SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND id>$2 ORDER BY id LIMIT $3"
    81	        } else {
    82	            "SELECT id,data FROM r WHERE t=$1 AND $2::text IS NULL ORDER BY id LIMIT $3"
    83	        };
    84	        let page=tx.query(query,&[&table,&after,&limit])?;
    85	        if adoption::page_fits(page.iter().map(|raw| raw.get::<_,&str>(1)), meter, work,
    86	            Some(&|row| adoption::contribution_bytes(row,schema)))? { return Ok(page); }
    87	        limit=(page.len() as i64/2).max(1);
    88	        drop(page);
    89	        meter.release_heap(page_mark.clone());
    90	    }
    91	}

     3	/-!
     4	# Maintained aggregate identity
     5	
     6	The executable engine uses SHA-256 over a domain-separated canonical group
     7	tuple. This independent model deliberately does not reproduce that
     8	cryptographic implementation. It models the properties the language and
     9	store protocols rely on: versioned domain separation, a 64-character
    10	lowercase-hex identity for every logical group (including the empty tuple),
    11	and adoption as one state transition that replaces every legacy physical
    12	identity while publishing the new version.
    13	-/
    14	
    15	namespace Quarry
    16	
    17	/-- The protocol domain whose change requires another store capability and
    18	migration. -/
    19	def maintainedIdDomainV1 : List Nat := cps "snapback4-maintained-id/sha256-v1"
    20	
    21	/-- A small independent digest abstraction. Its contents are intentionally
    22	not the engine's SHA-256; only its versioned input and fixed hex shape belong
    23	to this logical model. -/
    24	def maintainedIdV1 (key : Key) : List Nat :=
    25	  (List.range 64).map fun i =>
    26	    let nibble := (maintainedIdDomainV1.length + (encKey key).length + i) % 16
    27	    if nibble < 10 then 48 + nibble else 87 + nibble
    28	
    29	theorem maintainedIdV1_length (key : Key) : (maintainedIdV1 key).length = 64 := by
    30	  simp [maintainedIdV1]
    31	
    32	/-- The canonical tagged-id overhead is nine bytes and lowercase ASCII is one
    33	byte per character, so every maintained identity fits the 144-byte id bound. -/
    34	theorem maintainedIdV1_fits (key : Key) : 9 + (maintainedIdV1 key).length ≤ 144 := by
    35	  rw [maintainedIdV1_length]
    36	  omega
    37	
    38	def maintainedRowV1 (key : Key) (cols : List (String × Scalar)) : Row :=
    39	  { id := maintainedIdV1 key, cols }
    40	
    41	structure MaintainedState where
    42	  version : Nat
    43	  rows : List Row
    44	
    45	/-- Adoption rebuilds all reconstructible aggregate rows and publishes the
    46	identity version in the same pure state result. `old` is an input so the model
    47	states explicitly that legacy physical ids are never retained. -/
    48	def adoptMaintainedV1 (_old : MaintainedState)
    49	    (groups : List (Key × List (String × Scalar))) : MaintainedState :=
    50	  { version := 1, rows := groups.map fun group => maintainedRowV1 group.1 group.2 }
    51	
    52	theorem adoptMaintainedV1_version (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
    53	    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).version = 1 := rfl
    54	
    55	theorem adoptMaintainedV1_ids (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
    56	    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.id = groups.map fun group => maintainedIdV1 group.1 := by
    57	  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]
    58	
    59	theorem adoptMaintainedV1_values (old : MaintainedState) (groups) :
    60	    (adoptMaintainedV1 old groups).rows.map Row.cols = groups.map Prod.snd := by
    61	  simp [adoptMaintainedV1, maintainedRowV1]
    62	
    63	example : (maintainedIdV1 []).length = 64 := maintainedIdV1_length []
    64	example : (maintainedIdV1 [.id (List.replicate 64 97), .text (List.replicate 64 120)]).length = 64 :=
    65	  maintainedIdV1_length _
    66	
    67	end Quarry

diff --git a/llp/3000.007.003-the-engine-writes-derived-data.rfc.md b/llp/3000.007.003-the-engine-writes-derived-data.rfc.md

+++ b/llp/3000.007.003-the-engine-writes-derived-data.rfc.md
@@ -139,6 +139,12 @@ identity, and synthetic check rows, incremental writes, point reads and
 adoption rebuilds all call the same function. The group key remains the public
 address; programs do not read or supply this internal id.
 
+The intrinsic `byId` order of aggregate rows is consequently opaque digest
+order. It is stable for one identity version but has no relationship to the
+lexical or numeric order of group fields, and migration may change it. A query
+whose result needs group-key order declares that order explicitly (for example,
+`first 50 by .emoji`) rather than relying on an unqualified aggregate scan.
+
 The SQLite metadata and evaluation-PostgreSQL backend marker

 function. Opening or adopting either store without the marker — including a

+
+fn strip_maintained_identity_capability(mut wire: String) -> String {
+    let capability = "maintained-id-sha256-v1";
+    wire = wire.replace(&format!("\"{capability}\","), "")
+        .replace(&format!(",\"{capability}\""), "")
+        .replace(&format!("[{{\"Capabilities\":[\"{capability}\"]}}]"), "[]")
+        .replace(&format!("{{\"Capabilities\":[\"{capability}\"]}},"), "")
+        .replace(&format!(",{{\"Capabilities\":[\"{capability}\"]}}"), "");
+    assert!(!wire.contains(capability));
+    wire
 }

+writer/head fence. Before clearing targets, adoption derives each target's
+legacy-id-to-digest map to a fixed point over typed reference dependencies,
+then rewrites every surviving typed reference through those maps. Thus an
+aggregate grouped by a reference to another aggregate uses that referenced
+aggregate's new digest when deriving its own digest, and a table that refers
+to either rebuilt target does not dangle. A legacy id with no matching stored
+target stays opaque, preserving the existing dangling-reference contract.
+Reference rewrites, index updates, target rebuilds, marker and generation share
+the same transaction. Schemas with ordinary maintains require device capability
 `maintained-id-sha256-v1`; an older device is refused at the handshake before
 it can compute a legacy id and silently read a digest-addressed aggregate as
 zero.

+refusal in any of these retirements aborts the whole mutation, including
+earlier cascade and set-null writes.

+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn has_legacy_maintained_reference(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    match kind {
+        crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table } => ids.get(table).is_some_and(|ids| !ids.is_empty()),
+        crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner)
+        | crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of: inner, .. }
+        | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of: inner, .. } => has_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, ids),
+        _ => false,
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]
+fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(
+    kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType,
+    value: &mut Value,
+    ids: &BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>>,
+) -> bool {
+    match (kind, value) {
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Ref { table }, Value::Id(id)) => {
+            let Some(next) = ids.get(table).and_then(|ids| ids.get(id)) else { return false };
+            *id = next.clone();
+            true
+        }
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::Optional(inner), value) => rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(inner, value, ids),
+        (crate::schema::ColumnType::List { of, .. } | crate::schema::ColumnType::ListRange { of, .. }, Value::Array(values)) =>
+            values.iter_mut().fold(false, |changed, value| rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(of, value, ids) || changed),
+        _ => false,
+    }
+}

+    pub(crate) fn rewrite_legacy_maintained_references(&mut self, maintains: &[Maintain]) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
+        let mut legacy = Vec::new();
+        for maintain in maintains.iter().filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none()) {
+            let target = self.schema.tables[&maintain.target].clone();
+            let fields: Vec<_> = maintain.group_fields().into_iter().map(|field| {
+                let kind = target.columns.get(&field).expect("validated maintain group").clone();
+                (field, kind)
+            }).collect();
+            let mut rows = Vec::new();
+            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
+            loop {
+                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &maintain.target, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
+                if page.is_empty() { break; }
+                for (row, encoded) in page {
+                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
+                    let old = row.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
+                    let key = fields.iter().map(|(field, kind)| Ok((kind.clone(), row.field(field)?.clone())))
+                        .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, RuntimeError>>()?;
+                    rows.push((old, key));
+                }
+            }
+            legacy.push((maintain.target.clone(), rows));
+        }
+
+        let mut ids: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>> = BTreeMap::new();
+        let mut settled = false;
+        for _ in 0..=legacy.len() {
+            let mut next_ids: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, String>> = BTreeMap::new();
+            for (target, rows) in &legacy {
+                let target_ids = next_ids.entry(target.clone()).or_default();
+                for (old, key) in rows {
+                    let key: Vec<_> = key.iter().map(|(kind, value)| {
+                        let mut value = value.clone();
+                        rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &mut value, &ids);
+                        value
+                    }).collect();
+                    let next = maintained_id(&key);
+                    if old != &next { target_ids.insert(old.clone(), next); }
+                }
+            }
+            if next_ids == ids {
+                ids = next_ids;
+                settled = true;
+                break;
+            }
+            ids = next_ids;
+        }
+        if !settled {
+            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema("legacy aggregate identity references form a cycle".into()));
+        }
+
+        let references: Vec<_> = self.schema.tables.iter().filter_map(|(name, table)| {
+            let columns: Vec<_> = table.columns.iter().filter_map(|(column, kind)|
+                has_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, &ids).then(|| (column.clone(), kind.clone())))
+                .collect();
+            (!columns.is_empty()).then(|| (name.clone(), table.clone(), columns))
+        }).collect();
+        let mut rewritten = 0_u64;
+        for (name, table, columns) in references {
+            let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
+            loop {
+                let page = self.metered_scan(|runner, allowance| runner.tx.scan(allowance, &name, "byId", &[], &bounds, Dir::Asc, 256))?;
+                if page.is_empty() { break; }
+                for (old, encoded) in page {
+                    bounds.after = crate::key::decode(&encoded);
+                    let mut next = old.clone();
+                    let mut changed = false;
+                    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut next {
+                        for (column, kind) in &columns {
+                            let Some(value) = fields.get_mut(column) else { continue };
+                            changed |= rewrite_legacy_maintained_reference(kind, value, &ids);
+                        }
+                    }
+                    if changed {
+                        self.tx.put(&name, &table, &next, Some(&old))?;
+                        rewritten = rewritten.saturating_add(1);
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        Ok(rewritten)
+    }

Dispositions in §11); 2026-10-12 (revision 2: folds the delta round, GPT and Muse both NOT READY. The reservation is defined from schema-fixed closure bounds: closure identities, closure-skipping probes, read-through seeks and a physical allowance, with heap as a maximum. The published touched set includes every derived destination, and the reply omits every row the actions changed. Cascade and set null are refused into tables that feed a maintained sum, have any field-owned column, or belong to a timeline in any role. `set null` is refused where any rule hops through the column. A device needs the referencing group acquired, not only readable. The removal order follows cascade and `read through` edges, whose union must be acyclic. `check` names the read prerequisite where a deleter may not be a reader (`N_DELETE_NEEDS_READ`). Dispositions in §11); 2026-10-12 (revision 1: folds one blind round, GPT NOT READY and Muse READY WITH CHANGES. `on delete keep` is added for deliberate history. A delete evaluates its whole cascade closure before it refuses, so a diamond or a sibling reference never refuses spuriously, and the reported reference is chosen in schema order, never by hidden iteration order. `set null` may clear only a column that carries no authority anywhere in the schema. Every published trace of a delete with actions — touched tables, change footprints, event counts, the physical authorization allowance — is fixed by the schema. The reservation reuses the exported source-write price, so a device consumes the same price the server computes. A null-exempt cap never proves a population bound. Cascade and set null into append-only, field-owned or unpriced children are refused. The postcondition is scoped to the rows present when the delete runs. Dispositions in §11); 2026-10-12 (draft)

+#[test]
+fn read_through_closure_probe_is_admitted_before_a_low_ceiling_delete() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  public
+  delete <- allow
+table children:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 2 by root
+  public
+table grandchildren:
+  child: children on delete cascade
+  cap 2 by child
+  immutable child
+  read through .child
+mutation drop(id: roots):
+  delete roots[id]
+"#;
+    let world = || {
+        let mut e = engine(source);
+        e.seed_at([
+            ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("p"))])),
+            ("children".into(), object([("id", id("c")), ("root", id("p"))])),
+            ("grandchildren".into(), object([("id", id("g")), ("child", id("c"))])),
+        ], 0).unwrap();
+        e
+    };
+    let context = || Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::from([("id".into(), id("p"))])).at(100);
+    let mut complete = world();
+    let sent = complete.mutate("drop", None, context()).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(sent.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", sent.state);
+
+    let mut cut = world();
+    let mut ceilings = cut.ceilings();
+    ceilings.examined = sent.metered.examined - 1;
+    cut.set_ceilings(ceilings);
+    let refused = cut.mutate("drop", None, context()).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(refused.state, WriteState::Failed { ref why, .. } if why.code == "E_BOUND"), "{:?}", refused.state);
+    assert_eq!(cut.store().rows("roots").unwrap().len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(cut.store().rows("children").unwrap().len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(cut.store().rows("grandchildren").unwrap().len(), 1);
+}

+#[test]
+fn same_id_replacement_reloads_maintained_columns_after_cascade_retirement() {
+    let source = r#"
+table roots:
+  expiresAt: time ?
+  by byExpiry: expiresAt
+  expire at .expiresAt
+  childCount: count children by root
+  public
+  insert <- allow
+table children:
+  root: roots on delete cascade
+  cap 4 by root
+  public
+mutation replace():
+  insert roots {id: 'same', expiresAt: null}
+"#;
+    let mut e = engine(source);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("roots".into(), object([("id", id("same")), ("expiresAt", Value::Int(10))])),
+        ("children".into(), object([("id", id("child")), ("root", id("same"))])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(e.store().rows("roots").unwrap()[0].field("childCount").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+
+    let replaced = e.mutate("replace", None, Context::new("dev:alice", BTreeMap::new()).at(100)).unwrap();
+    assert!(matches!(replaced.state, WriteState::Sent { .. }), "{:?}", replaced.state);
+    let roots = e.store().rows("roots").unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(roots.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(roots[0].field("childCount").unwrap(), &Value::Int(0));
+    assert!(e.store().rows("children").unwrap().is_empty());
+}

   138	impl Schema {
   139	    pub fn supported_capabilities() -> Vec<String> { CAPABILITIES.iter().map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect() }
   140	    fn has_receipt_columns(&self) -> bool {
   141	        self.tables.iter().any(|(name, table)| table.maintained.keys().any(|field|
   142	            self.receipt_dependencies.get(name).is_some_and(|fields| fields.contains(field))))
   143	    }
   144	    pub fn required_capabilities(&self) -> BTreeSet<String> {
   145	        CAPABILITIES.iter().filter(|(_, needs)| needs(self)).map(|(name, _)| (*name).into()).collect()
   146	    }
   147	}
   148	
   149	impl Serialize for Schema {
   150	    fn serialize<S: Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {
   151	        let required = self.required_capabilities();
   152	        // The derive's field order, omissions and bytes are unchanged for
   153	        // ordinary schemas, including the serialized conformance corpus.
   154	        if required.is_empty() { return Wire::serialize(self, serializer); }
   155	        let mut wire = self.clone();
   156	        for table in wire.tables.values_mut() {
   157	            table.constraints.retain(|c| !matches!(c, Constraint::Recorded));
   158	        }
   159	        let mut carrier = wire.tables.first_entry().ok_or_else(||
   160	            serde::ser::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: required capabilities need a table carrier"))?;
   161	        carrier.get_mut().constraints.push(Constraint::Capabilities(required));
   162	        Wire::serialize(&wire, serializer)
   163	    }
   164	}
   165	
   166	impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Schema {
   167	    fn deserialize<D: Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {
   168	        // The private remote derive uses the ordinary
   169	        // streaming serde codec. No JSON-value or content-buffer replay.
   170	        let mut schema = Wire::deserialize(deserializer)?;
   171	        let mut declared = BTreeSet::new();
   172	        let mut carriers = 0;
   173	        let mut legacy = false;
   174	        for table in schema.tables.values_mut() {
   175	            let mut recorded = 0;
   176	            table.constraints.retain(|constraint| {
   177	                if let Constraint::Capabilities(names) = constraint {
   178	                    carriers += 1;
   179	                    declared.extend(names.iter().cloned());
   180	                    false
   181	                } else if matches!(constraint, Constraint::Recorded) {
   182	                    recorded += 1;
   183	                    false
   184	                } else { true }
   185	            });
   186	            if recorded > 1 || (recorded != 0 && table.recorded.is_empty()) {
   187	                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: invalid legacy Recorded marker"));
   188	            }
   189	            if recorded != 0 { legacy = true; declared.insert("recorded-attribution".into()); }
   190	        }
   191	        for name in &declared {
   192	            if !CAPABILITIES.iter().any(|(known, _)| name == known) {
   193	                return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: unsupported engine capability {name}; upgrade the engine/device")));
   194	            }
   195	        }
   196	        let mut required = schema.required_capabilities();
   197	        // @ref LLP 3000.022#14.3 — RY already serialized the dependency closure.
   198	        // RP stamps every emitted schema so old devices refuse its new prediction
   199	        // facts, but an RP reader must still open RY's kept backend/database.
   200	        // All other capabilities and the carrier shape remain exact.
   201	        let legacy_receipt_prediction = !declared.contains("receipt-derived-prediction-v1")
   202	            && required.remove("receipt-derived-prediction-v1");
   203	        // The price carrier can be absent in an old projection. Missing prices
   204	        // are fenced per program, rather than bricking a kept store.
   205	        for cap in ["source-write-reservations-v1", "source-write-reservations-v2"] {
   206	            if declared.contains(cap) { required.insert(cap.into()); }
   207	            else { required.remove(cap); }
   208	        }
   209	        // Stores written before the digest migration have no carrier for this
   210	        // capability. Admit that persisted schema for server-side rebuilding;
   211	        // its next serialization stamps the capability, so old devices refuse.
   212	        let mut legacy_semantic_capabilities = BTreeSet::new();
   213	        if !declared.contains("maintained-id-sha256-v1")
   214	            && required.remove("maintained-id-sha256-v1") {
   215	            legacy_semantic_capabilities.insert("maintained-id-sha256-v1".into());
   216	        }
   217	        // Kept pre-Wave-12 schemas need the server's new expiry action path,
   218	        // then stamp the device fence on their next published projection.
   219	        if !declared.contains("expiry-reference-actions-v1")
   220	            && required.remove("expiry-reference-actions-v1") {
   221	            legacy_semantic_capabilities.insert("expiry-reference-actions-v1".into());
   222	        }
   223	        // Before the shared fence, the binder emitted Recorded on F2 tables
   224	        // even when the same schema also declared timelines. Only that legacy
   225	        // representation infers its full requirements; modern carriers remain
   226	        // exact, including when mixed with a legacy marker.
   227	        if legacy && carriers == 0 {
   228	            // A legacy marker only covers the capabilities that predate the fence.
   229	            // New semantics must never inherit permission from this escape hatch.
   230	            declared = required.iter().filter(|name| matches!(name.as_str(),
   231	                "maintained-column" | "recorded-attribution" | "timeline" | "timeline-v2")).cloned().collect();
   232	        }
   233	        if declared != required || carriers + usize::from(legacy) != usize::from(!required.is_empty()) {
   234	            return Err(serde::de::Error::custom(format!("E_SCHEMA_CAPABILITY: schema requires {required:?}, but declares {declared:?} in {carriers} carriers")));
   235	        }
   236	        let had_prices = !schema.source_reservations.is_empty();
   237	        schema.prepare_receipt_dependencies();
   238	        // Opening an old blob preserves its wire shape. Complete visible
   239	        // declarations can still price a write on demand; hidden ones cannot.
   240	        if !had_prices { schema.source_reservations.clear(); }
   241	        schema.legacy_receipt_prediction = legacy_receipt_prediction
   242	            || (!declared.contains("source-write-reservations-v1") && !schema.receipts.is_empty());
   243	        schema.legacy_semantic_capabilities = legacy_semantic_capabilities.into();
   244	        Ok(schema)
   245	    }
   246	}

+/// The copied corpus is a frozen image of the pre-digest store. Translate
+/// maintained target identities at the adapter boundary so its logical values
+/// remain an oracle for the current address function. Other row ids retain
+/// their exact frozen spelling.
+fn legacy_maintained_ids(schema: &Schema, rows: &[ReceiptRow]) -> Result<BTreeMap<String, String>, String> {
+    let mut ids = BTreeMap::new();
+    for receipt in rows {
+        let Some(maintain) = schema.maintains.iter().find(|maintain| maintain.target == receipt.table && maintain.row_key.is_none()) else { continue };
+        let old = match receipt.row.field("id") {
+            Ok(Value::Id(id)) => id,
+            Ok(_) => return Err(format!("{}.id is not an id", receipt.table)),
+            Err(error) => return Err(format!("{}.id: {error}", receipt.table)),
+        };
+        let key = maintain.by.iter().map(|field| receipt.row.field(field).cloned().map_err(|error| format!("{}.{}: {error}", receipt.table, field))).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?;
+        let new = snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&key);
+        if let Some(prior) = ids.insert(old.clone(), new.clone())
+            && prior != new
+        {
+            return Err(format!("legacy id {old} names more than one maintained group"));
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(ids)
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_row(schema: &Schema, table: &str, row: &mut Value, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) {
+    if !schema.maintains.iter().any(|maintain| maintain.target == table && maintain.row_key.is_none()) { return; }
+    let (Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields)) = row else { return };
+    let Some(Value::Id(id)) = fields.get_mut("id") else { return };
+    if let Some(replacement) = ids.get(id) {
+        *id = replacement.clone();
+    }
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_expected(expected: &mut Expected, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) -> Result<(), String> {
+    if ids.is_empty() || expected.error_code.is_some() { return Ok(()); }
+    let Some(canonical) = &expected.canonical_result else { return Ok(()) };
+    let mut value: Value = serde_json::from_str(canonical).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
+    translate_legacy_maintained_result(&mut value, ids);
+    expected.canonical_result = Some(snapback4_core::value::canonical_json(&value));
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+fn translate_legacy_maintained_result(value: &mut Value, ids: &BTreeMap<String, String>) {
+    match value {
+        Value::Id(id) => {
+            if let Some(replacement) = ids.get(id) {
+                *id = replacement.clone();
+            }
+        }
+        Value::Array(values) => values.iter_mut().for_each(|value| translate_legacy_maintained_result(value, ids)),
+        Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) => fields.values_mut().for_each(|value| translate_legacy_maintained_result(value, ids)),
+        _ => {}
+    }
+}

diff --git a/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..3708ad4a5a
--- /dev/null
+++ b/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/engine/postgres/maintained_identity_upgrade.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+//! Atomic adoption of the maintained-row address function in the evaluation
+//! adapter. The marker and generation publish in the same writer transaction
+//! as the target rebuild, so no writer can observe mixed legacy/digest ids.
+use super::*;
+
+pub(super) fn install(
+    tx: &store::Tx<'_>,
+    schema: &Schema,
+    creating: bool,
+    generation: u64,
+) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
+    let current = tx.query(
+        "SELECT maintained_identity_version FROM _backend WHERE singleton",
+        &[],
+    )?[0].get::<_, Option<&str>>(0).map(str::to_owned);
+    if current.as_deref() == Some(crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION) {
+        return Ok(generation);
+    }
+
+    let aggregates: Vec<_> = schema.maintains.iter()
+        .filter(|maintain| maintain.private.is_none() && maintain.row_key.is_none())
+        .cloned()
+        .collect();
+    if !creating && !aggregates.is_empty() {
+        let mut runner = Runner::new(
+            tx,
+            schema,
+            Context::system().at(crate::now_ms()),
+            Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort),
+            tx.next_seq()?,
+        );
+        runner.event_free = true;
+        for maintain in &aggregates {
+            runner.rebuild_maintain(maintain)?;
+        }
+    }
+
+    let generation = if creating || aggregates.is_empty() {
+        generation
+    } else {
+        generation.checked_add(1)
+            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Generation("generation overflow".into()))?
+    };
+    tx.execute(
+        "UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=$1, generation=$2 WHERE singleton",
+        &[&crate::schema::MAINTAINED_ID_VERSION, &store::signed(generation)?],
+    )?;
+    Ok(generation)
+}

+#[test]
+#[ignore = "requires isolated local Postgres; scripts/test-postgres.sh"]
+fn reopening_legacy_maintained_ids_rebuilds_before_publishing_the_generation() {
+    let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), r#"
+table entries:
+  bucket: int
+  public
+view totals: count entries by .bucket
+  public
+"#.into())]);
+    assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
+    let schema: Schema = serde_json::from_str(&serde_json::to_string(&bound.schema).unwrap()).unwrap();
+    let programs = bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program).collect::<Vec<_>>();
+    let url = std::env::var("SNAPBACK4_EVAL_POSTGRES").expect("private test-postgres.sh database");
+    let name = format!("sb4_eval_maintained_id_{:x}", crate::ids::seed());
+    let mut engine = PostgresEngine::create(Client::connect(&url, postgres::NoTls).unwrap(), &name, schema, programs).unwrap();
+    engine.load([("entries".into(), object([("id", Value::Id("entry".into())), ("bucket", Value::Int(7))]))]).unwrap();
+    let digest = crate::schema::maintained_id(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let legacy = crate::value::canonical_json(&[Value::Int(7)]);
+    let target = engine.schema.tables["totals"].clone();
+    let generation = engine.generation();
+    let tx = engine.store.transaction(Some(WriteMode::Serialized)).unwrap();
+    let old = tx.get("totals", &digest).unwrap().expect("current aggregate");
+    tx.delete("totals", &target, &old).unwrap();
+    let mut old = old;
+    if let Value::Row(fields) | Value::Map(fields) = &mut old {
+        fields.insert("id".into(), Value::Id(legacy.clone()));
+    }
+    tx.put("totals", &target, &old, None).unwrap();
+    tx.execute("UPDATE _backend SET maintained_identity_version=NULL WHERE singleton", &[]).unwrap();
+    tx.commit().unwrap();
+    drop(engine);
+
+    let mut reopened = PostgresEngine::open(Client::connect(&url, postgres::NoTls).unwrap(), &name).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(reopened.generation(), generation + 1);
+    let tx = reopened.store.transaction(None).unwrap();
+    assert!(tx.get("totals", &legacy).unwrap().is_none());
+    let rebuilt = tx.get("totals", &digest).unwrap().expect("digest aggregate");
+    assert_eq!(rebuilt.field("value").unwrap(), &Value::Int(1));
+    tx.rollback().unwrap();
+}

 fn run<H: Host>(host: &mut H) {
+    // Digest-addressed maintained rows use the same fixed identity on the
+    // server and each device store, even for the largest composite values in
+    // this generated family.
+    let aggregate = r#"
+table groups:
+  public
+  sync public
+table entries:
+  owner: principal
+  parent: groups
+  token: text <=64
+  amount: int
+  public
+  sync public
+view totals: sum entries of .amount by .owner, .parent, .token
+  public
+"#;
+    let (mut e, b) = compile(aggregate);
+    let principal = "p".repeat(64);
+    let parent = "r".repeat(64);
+    let token = "x".repeat(64);
+    e.seed_at([
+        ("groups".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([("id", id(&parent))])),
+        ("entries".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
+            ("id", id("entry")), ("owner", id(&principal)), ("parent", id(&parent)),
+            ("token", snapback4_core::Value::String(token.clone())),
+            ("amount", snapback4_core::Value::Int(7)),
+        ])),
+    ], 0).unwrap();
+    let expected = snapback4_core::schema::maintained_id(&[
+        id(&principal), id(&parent), snapback4_core::Value::String(token),
+    ]);
+    assert_eq!(expected.len(), 64);
+    let mut d = host.open("aggregate-digest", Some(b)).unwrap();
+    acquire(&mut e, &mut d, &principal, 0);
+    let rows = d.store().raw_rows("totals");
+    assert_eq!(rows.len(), 1);
+    assert_eq!(rows[0].field("id").unwrap(), &id(&expected));
+    host.close("aggregate-digest", d);
+
     // Server expiry is a physical retirement with the schema's declared
     // referential effects. Devices receive that one committed closure just as
     // they receive an authored parent delete.
